title: Sammy Price's Bluesicians recordings in Paris
summary: They discuss the Dec 1955 to Feb 1956 Paris dates and Moore's vocals.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, with Sam Price, Sam Price and His Bluesicians. He recorded under that name, and apparently on December 29, 1955, he recorded with you, Pops Foster, Herbie Hill...
What year was that?
1955. Emmett Berry was on trumpet, and George Stevenson was on trombone, and Herb Hall was on clarinet. How long were you with Sam Price? It was just for that tour, you were saying.
Just that tour, yes.

And you recorded over there. Did that tour go into early 1956, or was this a different tour? Apparently, there was another series of recordings made in Paris during January and February 1956, that involved you and that same band. There were a lot of recordings. "Swingin' Kansas
Moore (III) - 80
City Style," "New Shoes Blues"...
I was singing a vocal on that.
You had a vocal on that?
Yes.

These were released in Paris, Club Francais Du Disque, #63 and Guild Du Jazz... There's also "Shorty Needs Mademoiselle," "Fontainebleau Boogie"... "Fred's Basement Boogie," what's that? That was never issued. But was that yours?
What was that one?
"Fred's Basement Boogie." Is that something of yours?
I don't know. They'd probably run out of names. I don't know whether I was on that or not. '56?
'56, yeah. This is February we're talking about, January and February.
With the same band.

Same band, yeah. Emmett Berry, George Stevenson, Herbie Hall, Sammy Price, Pops Foster, Fred Moore. A series of recordings made between December 1955, January 1956, and February 1956. Well, we don't have them. We'll have to see if we can track some of those recordings down and put them on tape for you. It may, of course, take a while. Some of them may not even be available in this
Moore (III) - 81
country. It looks like they were French releases. And so on and so forth.
Now, after that tour with Sammy Price... Sam Price is a Blues musician, he plays a lot of Boogie-Woogie. Did you enjoy playing with him?
Yeah! Good piano player.
